t: A Baptist minister's son from Atlanta, King became the best-known spokesman of the civil rights movement after leading the Montgomery bus boycott, which lasted 385 days and ended with a ruling against segregated buses.

Through the Southern Christian Leadership Conference he led nonviolent campaigns at Birmingham, in Selma and elsewhere, and the movement won legislative gains in the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and the Fair Housing Act of 1968.

In his last years he opposed the Vietnam War and poverty, lost allies for doing so, was surveilled by the FBI, and was shot dead in Memphis on 4 April 1968 while supporting striking sanitation workers.
dyk: King was born Michael King Jr. In 1934, after a trip that took his father to Berlin and to sites in Germany linked to the Reformation leader Martin Luther, the father changed his own name, and his five-year-old son's, to Martin Luther King.
ev: Born in Atlanta, Georgia, the second of three children of a Baptist minister and his wife
Graduates from Morehouse College with a Bachelor of Arts in sociology, aged nineteen
Receives his PhD from Boston University and leads the Montgomery bus boycott, which lasts 385 days
Helps found the Southern Christian Leadership Conference and becomes its first president
Writes the Letter from Birmingham Jail and delivers the I Have a Dream speech at the March on Washington
Becomes the youngest winner of the Nobel Peace Prize; the Civil Rights Act is passed
Leads marchers to the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma and speaks at the end of the march to Montgomery
Shot at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis on 4 April and dies the same evening

f.born: 15 January 1929 in Atlanta, Georgia, as Michael King Jr.; second of three children of the Baptist minister Michael King and Alberta King (née Williams); his name was changed in 1934 to Martin Luther King Jr.
f.died: 4 April 1968 in Memphis, Tennessee; shot by James Earl Ray at the Lorraine Motel at 6:01 p.m. and pronounced dead at St. Joseph's Hospital at 7:05 p.m.; his remains were moved in 1977 to a tomb at what is now the Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
f.role: Baptist minister; pastor of Dexter Avenue Baptist Church, Montgomery (from 1954); leader of the Montgomery bus boycott (1955–1956); first president of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (1957–1968); co-pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church, Atlanta (from 1960)
f.known: the Montgomery bus boycott; nonviolent protest against Jim Crow laws; the Birmingham campaign and the Letter from Birmingham Jail; the 1963 March on Washington and the I Have a Dream speech; the Selma voting rights marches; the 1964 Nobel Peace Prize; opposition to the Vietnam War and the Poor People's Campaign
